newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arab Bank still considering bonus share.
newsitem.headline: Arab Bank still considering bonus share.

text.p: Arab Bank chairman Abdulmajeed Shoman said on Friday the bank was still considering issuing bonus shares to shareholders but would wait for ratification of a law cancelling a 15 percent tax on capital increases.

Shoman sidestepped calls from shareholders attending the bank's annual general meeting to set a date for the long-planned bonus issue, which would be funded by a transfer of cash from reserves into the bank's paid-up capital.
"When the law is issued we are ready to call an extraordinary general meeting to discuss it," he said.

The bank's stock slipped to 250 dinars from 269 dinars in the last two weeks as investors worried it might be abandoning plans for the bonus shares. The stock recovered slightly at the end of weekly trade on Wednesday to 256 dinars.
Jordan's parliament has passed a law cancelling the 15 percent tax on capital raises, but it has yet to be formally ratified.
